Title: Forward masking among infant and adult listeners.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz tone probe; broadband noise forward masker
Outcome: Infants showed more forward masking than adults, especially at short masker-probe intervals
Evidence_Quote: Listeners detected a repeated 1000-Hz probe, with 16-ms rise time, no steady-state duration, and 16-ms fall time. Unmasked thresholds were determined for one group of listeners who were trained to respond when they heard the probe but not at other times. In the masking conditions, each tone burst was preceded by a 100-ms broadband noise masker at 65 dB SPL

Title: Basic properties of the sound-evoked post-auricular muscle response (PAMR).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: human subjects incl. very young infants (ages not specified)
Stimulus_Type: click and tone-burst stimuli (post-auricular muscle response)
Outcome: PAMR basic properties described; infant responses reach adult values by 12 months
Evidence_Quote: It can be obtained with click and tone-burst stimuli within 20 dB of the subjective detection threshold, can be evoked with tone-bursts between 500 Hz and 16 kHz and grows either linearly with the click level or approximately exponentially with the tone-burst level, reaching a maximum of as large as 250 microV pp in some subjects. It has a frequency spectrum mostly between 25 and 200 Hz.

Title: Infants' sensitivity to broadband noise.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Infant-adult threshold differences smaller for broadband noise than for tones
Evidence_Quote: Unmasked and masked thresholds for a 1000-Hz tone and for broadband noise were estimated adaptively for infants and adults using an observer-based behavioral procedure.

Title: Maturation of cochlear nonlinearity as measured by distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression growth in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: adults, children, term-born and premature neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones with suppressor tones
Outcome: Neonates showed shallower suppression growth and elevated suppression thresholds for low-frequency suppressors
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression growth was measured at two f2 frequencies (1500 and 6000 Hz) and three primary tone levels (55-45, 65-55, and 75-65 dB SPL).

Title: Development of f2/f1 ratio functions in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: pre-term infants, term infants, and young adults
Outcome: Optimal f2/f1 ratio and Q3 showed age x frequency interactions; cochlear mechanisms still maturing at term
Evidence_Quote: Frequency ratio functions were analyzed at three f2 frequencies--2000, 4000 and 6000 Hz.

Title: Middle ear development. I: Extra-stapedius response in the neonatal chick.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: sound stimuli (extra-stapedius velocity by laser interferometry)
Outcome: Low-frequency sensitivity increased by 11 dB with age; no consistent high-frequency improvement
Evidence_Quote: The ES velocity and phase responses in the frequency range between 0.2 and 10.0 kHz were measured in animals ranging from 3 days of age to adult.

Title: Influence of swaddling on sleep and arousal characteristics of healthy infants.
Journal: Pediatrics
Stimulus_Type: white noise of increasing intensity (arousal threshold test)
Outcome: Swaddling increased sleep efficiency, but lower-intensity stimuli induced cortical arousals during REM sleep
Evidence_Quote: In both conditions, the infants were exposed to white noise of increasing intensity, from 50 to 100 dB(A), during rapid eye movement sleep, to determine their arousal thresholds.

Title: Maturation of the cortical auditory evoked potential in infants and young children.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborns (<7 days), toddlers (13-41 months), children (4-6 years), adults (18-45 years)
Stimulus_Type: 400 Hz and 3000 Hz tones and word token /baed/
Outcome: CAEP component latencies and amplitudes mature from birth to adulthood
Evidence_Quote: CAEPs were obtained in response to low (400 Hz) and high (3000 Hz) tones and to the word token /baed/, all presented at 60 dB HL, at a rate of 0.22 Hz.

Title: Theory of forward and reverse middle-ear transmission applied to otoacoustic emissions in infant and adult ears.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no new subjects (theory; prior data from infants through 6 months and adults)
Outcome: Larger infant DPOAE levels attributed mainly to reverse middle-ear transmittance varying with ear-canal area
Evidence_Quote: In a previous study, distortion product (DP) OAE input/output (I/O) functions were shown to differ at f2 = 6 kHz in adults compared to infants through 6 months of age.

Title: In vivo ultrasonic attenuation slope estimates for detecting cervical ripening in rats: Preliminary results.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: rats (pregnant, in vivo; ex vivo cervix)
Outcome: No significant effect of ultrasonic attenuation with gestational age in vivo
Evidence_Quote: Spherically-focused f/3 transducers with 33-MHz center frequencies and with 9-mm focal lengths were used in both the simulations and experiments.

Title: Effects of maturation on tympanometric wideband acoustic transfer functions in human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: wideband acoustic transfer function measurements at varying static ear-canal pressures
Outcome: Energy reflectance and admittance showed frequency-dependent developmental changes with ear-canal pressure
Evidence_Quote: For frequencies from 0.25 to 0.75 kHz there was as much as a 30% change in mean ER and mid |Y| with changes in static ear-canal pressure between 4 and 24 weeks of age. From 0.75 to 2 kHz, the effects of pressure produced a small number of significant differences in ER and mid |Y| with age, suggestive of a developmentally stable frequency range. Between 2 and 6 kHz, there were differential effects of pressure for the youngest infants; negative pressures caused increased ER and mid |Y| and positive pressures caused decreased ER and mid |Y|; the magnitude of this effect decreased with age.

Title: Methods for estimating infant thresholds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Thresholds similar across estimation techniques; constant stimuli least variable
Evidence_Quote: Detection thresholds for 1000-Hz, 16-ms tone bursts were estimated for 3- and 6-month-old infants and for young adults.

Title: Auditory processing during sleep in preterm infants: An event related potential study.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: premature infants (mean GA 30 weeks; post-conceptional age 35 weeks)
Stimulus_Type: oddball tones: standard 1000 Hz, deviant 2000 Hz
Outcome: Deviant-tone frontal negativity (200-300 ms) present only in active sleep
Evidence_Quote: frequently occurring 'standard' tones at 1000Hz and infrequent 'deviant' tones at 2000Hz.

Title: Six-month-old infants discriminate voicing on the basis of temporal envelope cues (L).
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech tokens /aba/ and /apa/ with envelope information below 64 Hz
Outcome: Infants discriminated voicing from temporal envelope cues alone
Evidence_Quote: processed to retain envelope information below 64 Hz while degrading temporal fine structure cues.

Title: Increased heating by diagnostic ultrasound due to nonlinear propagation.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Nonlinear propagation enhanced heating (up to about 3x); maximum temperature rise 2 degrees C
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made of the temperature rise in a sample of tissue-mimicking gel, caused by the application of 3.6-MHz focused ultrasonic beams for 3 min.

Title: Perception of missing fundamental pitch by 3- and 4-month-old human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: missing-fundamental harmonic complexes; masking noise; bandpass filtering
Outcome: Infants categorized complexes by missing-fundamental pitch
Evidence_Quote: This study investigated the ability of 3- and 4-month-olds to perceive the pitch of MF harmonic complexes based on fundamentals of 160 Hz and 200 Hz using an observer-based method. In experiment I, to demonstrate MF pitch discrimination, 3- and 4-month-olds were required to ignore spectral changes in complexes with the same fundamental and to respond only when the fundamental changed. In experiment II, a 60-260 Hz noise was presented with complexes to mask combination tones at the fundamental frequency. In experiment III, complexes were bandpass filtered with a -12 dB/octave slope to limit use of spectral edge cues and presented with a pink noise to mask all distortion products.

Title: Preliminary evaluation of a two-interval, two-alternative infant behavioral testing procedure.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Two-interval forced-choice procedure feasible and efficient in infants
Evidence_Quote: Ten of 11 infants (7-9 months of age) achieved a criterion of 80%-correct detection of a 50-dB sound pressure level noise band in a single testing session.

Title: Modified spectral tilt affects infants' native-language discrimination of approximants and vowels.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds /r/-/l/ and vowels with spectral tilt
Outcome: 6-month-olds discriminated spectrally modified sounds; 9-month-olds only unmodified
Evidence_Quote: Infants were presented with /r/-/l/ and /ɔ/-/ɐ/ in three conditions: (a) unmodified; (b) -6 dB/octave tilt; and (c) +6 dB/octave tilt.

Title: Discrimination of frequency transitions by human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1.0-kHz pulsed-tone standard with linear frequency transitions
Outcome: Frequency-sweep DLs about 3-4%; brief sweeps harder to discriminate
Evidence_Quote: Difference limens (DLs) for linear frequency transitions using a 1.0-kHz pulsed-tone standard were obtained from 6- to 9-month-old human infants in a series of three experiments.

Title: Phonetic enhancement of Mandarin vowels and tones: Infant-directed speech and Lombard speech.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Vowel space expanded in IDS and Lombard speech; tone space expansion only in IDS
Evidence_Quote: Vowel and tone productions were produced by 15 Mandarin-speaking mothers during interactions with their 12-month-old infants during a play session (IDS), in conversation with a Mandarin-speaking adult in a 70 dBA eight-talker babble noise environment (Lombard speech), and in a quiet environment (adult-directed speech).

Title: Ontogeny of auditory brainstem responses in the bat, Phyllostomus discolor.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: bats (Phyllostomus discolor), juveniles (p7 to p200) and adults
Outcome: Juveniles responsive up to 90 kHz by p7; hearing sensitivity increases until about p14
Evidence_Quote: measured auditory brainstem responses (ABRs) to clicks and narrowband tone pips covering a large frequency range (5-90 kHz) in juveniles (p7 to p200) and adults of the bat, Phyllostomus discolor.

Title: The influence of developmental noise exposure on the temporal processing of acoustical signals in the auditory cortex of rats.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: Long Evans rats (exposed on postnatal day 14)
Outcome: Developmental noise exposure permanently altered temporal and rate coding in auditory cortex
Evidence_Quote: The animals were exposed on postnatal day 14 (P14) for 12 minutes to a loud (125 dB SPL) broad-band noise.

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human adults and infants: wave V tuning curves.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: third-octave-filtered click probes with tonal maskers
Outcome: Infant wave V tuning curves broader (smaller tip-to-tail, lower Q10) for high-frequency probes
Evidence_Quote: Probe stimuli were 1.0, 4.0, and 8.0-kHz third-octave-filtered clicks.

Title: Level and age effects in infant frequency discrimination.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones at 40 and 80 dB sensation level
Outcome: Infant FDLs worse than adults except at 4000 Hz for 6- and 12-month-olds
Evidence_Quote: Frequency difference limens (FDLs) were estimated for 3-, 6-, and 12-month-old infants and for adults using pure tones at 500, 1000, and 4000 Hz. Each listener provided an FDL at 40 dB and at a higher (80 dB, in most cases) sensation level (SL).

Title: Neural processing of auditory temporal modulations in awake infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: awake infants (3 and 10 months) and young adults
Outcome: AMFR observable at 8 Hz at all ages; reliable 40 Hz responses only in adults
Evidence_Quote: in awake infants (3- and 10-month-olds) and awake young adults and for both slow and faster modulation rates (8 and 40 Hz).

Title: Infant pitch perception: evidence for responding to pitch categories and the missing fundamental.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Infants showed perceptual constancy and missing-fundamental pitch perception
Evidence_Quote: demonstrated the ability to discriminate harmonic complexes from two pitch categories that differed in pitch by approximately 20% (e.g., 160 vs 200 Hz).

Title: TRPA1 deficiency affects cochlear potentials days after noise exposure.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: clicks and 8 kHz tone bursts (ABR); noise exposure
Outcome: TRPA1 deficiency altered summating potentials and rCM after noise exposure
Evidence_Quote: mice exhibited a direct current (DC) shift in the rCM elicited by an 8 kHz tone burst as the sound intensity increased, which was delayed in Trpa1-/- mice.

Title: Binaural interactions in cortical area AI of cats reared with unilateral atresia of the external ear canal.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: adult cats reared with unilateral ear-canal atresia
Stimulus_Type: tones via sealed calibrated acoustic system (no numeric values stated)
Outcome: Binaural interaction classes normal; IID sensitivity shifted for the atretic ear

Title: Frequency and age-dependent auditory evoked potential thresholds in infants.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: Largest infant-adult threshold difference at 4.0 kHz, decreasing with age
Evidence_Quote: Auditory evoked-potential thresholds to 0.5, 4.0 and 10.0 kHz tone pips were measured in 40 normal infants 2-28 wks old and 14 normal hearing adults. Thresholds to 500 Hz tone pips were based upon the steady-state, 40 Hz evoked potential.

Title: Infants' discrimination of intensity variation in multisyllabic stimuli.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: synthetic CVC syllables with peak-intensity increments
Outcome: Infants discriminated intensity increments of 2 dB and above; better in bisyllabic context
Evidence_Quote: Discrimination performance was above chance for a 2-dB increment, and improved for 4- and 6-dB increments.

Title: Infants' pitch perception: inharmonic tonal complexes.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic and inharmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental)
Outcome: Infants discriminated pitch of inharmonic complexes; performance fell with stronger inharmonicity
Evidence_Quote: infants demonstrated the ability to discriminate two harmonic complexes based on missing fundamental frequencies of 160 and 200 Hz.

Title: The development of frequency resolution in humans as revealed by the auditory brain-stem response recorded with notched-noise masking.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Tuning adultlike by 6 months; 3-month-olds immature at 8000 Hz
Evidence_Quote: Tone-pip stimuli at 1000, 4000, and 8000 Hz (50 dB nHL) were presented simultaneously with notched-noise masking centered at frequencies related to the tone-pip frequency (1/3-oct intervals above and below the probe frequency).

Title: Noise induced hearing loss in fetal sheep.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: broadband noise exposure; clicks and tone bursts via bone oscillator
Outcome: Noise exposure temporarily elevated fetal ABR thresholds by an average of 8 dB
Evidence_Quote: The auditory brainstem response (ABR) was recorded in utero from chronically instrumented fetal sheep prior to and following exposure of pregnant ewes to intense broadband noise (120 dB SPL for 16 h). ABRs were elicited by clicks and tone bursts (0.5, 1, 2, and 4 kHz) delivered through a bone oscillator secured to the fetal skull.

Title: Aspects of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions in healthy newborns.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: SOAE prevalence 78%; levels between -2 and 42 dB SPL; most emissions above 2 kHz
Evidence_Quote: The SOAE levels were between -2 and 42 dB SPL. The mean level per emitting ear was 8.0 dB SPL and not significantly different between right and left ears or genders. However, the level of the strongest emission per emitting ear was significantly higher for right than for left ears. In contrast with adults most of the emissions (70%) are at frequencies above 2 kHz.

Title: Simultaneous masking in newborn chickens.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: Simultaneous masking patterns mature at hatching; no developmental change
Evidence_Quote: In the first experiment data were collected with a 500-Hz masker presented at 15 or 25 dB above absolute threshold.

Title: The relationship between auditory brainstem response and behavioral thresholds in normal hearing infants and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: Infant ABR thresholds adultlike at all frequencies; behavioral thresholds elevated relative to adults
Evidence_Quote: Thresholds were estimated for tone pips at 1, 4, and 8 kHz, presented at a rate of 13.3/s.

Title: Decreased cardiac responses to auditory stimulation during prone sleep.
Journal: Pediatrics
Outcome: Prone sleep decreased cardiac responses to auditory stimulation
Evidence_Quote: Their behavioral and cardiac responses were recorded during rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, both before and after exposure to 90 dB (A) of white-noise.

Title: The cochlear place-frequency map of the adult and developing Mongolian gerbil.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: Mongolian gerbils (adult and subadult, 18 days after birth)
Outcome: Cochlear place-frequency map established; slope 1.5 mm/octave; map shifts during maturation
Evidence_Quote: The map was established for frequencies between 0.3 and 31.9 kHz.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) amplitude as a function of f2/f1 frequency ratio and primary tone level separation in human adults and neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: Optimal f2/f1 ratio comparable in adults and neonates; level-separation effects differed for premature neonates
Evidence_Quote: Two f2 frequencies were investigated: 1500 and 6000 Hz.

Title: Features of the auditory development of the short-tailed Brazilian opossum, Monodelphis domestica: evoked responses, neonatal vocalizations and synapses in the inferior colliculus.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: Hearing onset at postnatal day 24 (threshold 83 dB SPL), declining to below 58 dB by day 40
Evidence_Quote: Evoked potentials were first recorded at postnatal day 24 at a threshold of 83 dB SPL; thresholds declined over subsequent weeks to below 58 dB at 40 days. Isolation calls emitted by the pups had stereotypic spectra with peaks at near 13 kHz and an octave higher.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions in human newborns and adults. I. Frequency effects.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human newborns (term and preterm) and adults
Outcome: Newborn 2f1-f2 DPOAE amplitudes larger than adults at lower frequencies
Evidence_Quote: At the highest frequencies assessed (f2 = 4.2-9.9 kHz) all subjects had similar amplitude 2 f1-f2 DPOAEs. At lower frequencies adult 2 f1-f2 amplitudes were significantly less than those of newborns. At the lowest frequencies reliably assessed (f2 = 1.5-2.1 kHz) term newborns had significantly larger 2 f1-f2 DPOAEs than preterm newborns.

Title: Postnatal development of the organ of Corti in cats: a light microscopic morphometric study.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: kittens (P1, P5, P10, P15) and adult cats
Stimulus_Type: none (light-microscopic morphometry; cochlear locations by adult best frequency)
Outcome: Postnatal development of organ of Corti morphology characterized
Evidence_Quote: Measurements were made of the organ of Corti at 3 cochlear locations: 20%, 60% and 85% of basilar membrane length from the base cochlear locations which in the adult correspond to best frequencies of approximately 20 kHz, 2 kHz and 500 Hz, respectively.
